biography:
Panixphere is a British mathcore and experimental punk-rock band associated with the fertile musical circle surrounding Cardiacs. Formed in the 1980s, the group has been led consistently by guitarist and vocalist Christian “Bic” Hayes, while its shifting lineups have included musicians connected with Cardiacs, Levitation, Dark Star, Dragons, and The Wildhearts. Their performances became known for speed, abrasive energy, irregular structures, and a deliberately chaotic edge, placing them in a distinctive position between punk, metal, and avant-garde rock.

Panixphere’s early activity was followed by a 1990s revival featuring Cardiacs members Tim Smith and Jon Poole alongside drummer David Francolini, with the band appearing at prominent British psychedelic and alternative-music events. Although their recorded output was long scarce, Panixphere contributed a Cardiacs cover to the 2010 compilation Leader of the Starry Skies: A Loyal Companion and issued the split release CONFINEMENT/release6 with Spratleys Japs in 2020. Later performances and recordings—including the album Gods & Zeros—have expanded the group’s legacy, documenting a band whose lean, fast, technically intricate music helped connect the Cardiacs tradition to mathcore’s angular intensity.

lastfm.bio_content: Panixphere is/was a British rock band featuring various past, present and future members of Cardiacs and Levitation, Dark Star, Dragons and The Wildhearts. The band's only consistent member has been guitarist and singer Christian "Bic" Hayes. The 1982-1984 lineup also featured “Flat Hat” and future Cardiacs roadie “Little Hicky”. The 1992-1993 lineup also featured Tim Smith (bass, vocals), Jon Poole (guitar, vocals) and David Francolini (drums). Despite being formed in the 1980s, Panixphere's only official releases was a Cardiacs cover on the compilation Leader of the Starry Skies: A Loyal Companion, released in 2010 and a split single with Spratleys Japs, CONFINEMENT/release6, released in 2020. Panixphere also performed several high-profile concerts on the British psychedelic music scene during the 1990s, some of which were bootlegged and distributed by fans. Read more on Last.fm.
